doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Panama City, Bert Massengale, Bill Bennett's club and LSU
summary: Panken runs through jobs along the Gulf, his marriage on New Year's 1951 and enrolling at LSU.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, after that, you went to Lafayette, Louisiana, and you got a three-week job there. Then the trio broke up. Then you went to Panama City, Florida, and you took a job there, and stuff happened. You played trumpet and piano, and the pianist Walter Norris was also playing piano—who would wind up playing with Ornette Coleman on his first record, and settled in Europe, and was a first-class jazz concert pianist.

All sorts of adventures throughout the South. Then you got a job with a territory band led by Bert Massengale, also playing a lot of trumpet, but later moving to piano. Then is when you met Bill Bennett, in Jackson, Mississippi. That was mid 1950...
It says you spent a lot of time playing at Bill Bennett’s club, among other places, until you moved to New York in 1956.

Whilst playing at Bill Bennett’s club, I think the day after New Year’s Eve in 1951, the two of you are married, and you then applied to LSU, and enrolled there as an English major, and you made Baton Rouge your base for the next number of years. It seems that your experience at LSU was crucial in forming your mature sensibility, crystallizing a lot of the different threads you’d been working with while perhaps not really thinking about it.
Yeah. Well, I was working with Lee Fortier. He had lots of bands.
You also worked a little club on weekends. Feets or something like that.
